info.name: AFAQY — Report Data (full chain)
info.description:
Retrieving actual report values from the AFAQY API, end to end.

WHY THE CATALOG HAS NO VALUES
/reports/lists and /user_report_templates/lists return report *definitions*: the column names, codes, formats and aggregation. They describe the report; they never run it. That is why the response looks like metadata — it is.

THE FOUR CALLS THAT PRODUCE VALUES
  1. POST /user_reports/add          creates the run, returns the report id
  2. POST /user_reports/percentage   generation progress — poll until it is 100
  3. POST /user_reports/data-summary the aggregated summary, one row per vehicle
  4. POST /user_reports/data-new     the detail behind one vehicle, by resource_id

STEP 2 IS THE ONE PEOPLE MISS
The report is generated asynchronously. Reading the rows immediately after creating it returns an empty data array with status_code 200 and message "success" — a valid response that looks like a failure. Poll the percentage first; nine times out of ten an empty report simply had not finished.

HOW TO USE THIS COLLECTION
  · Open the collection Variables tab and fill in username and password, or paste a token directly.
  · Optionally put an IMEI in the imei variable to target a specific vehicle.
  · Set date_from and date_to (YYYY-MM-DD).
  · Run the requests in order, or use the Postman Runner — the token, user_id, unit_id and report_id are captured automatically between steps, and request 4 loops until generation completes.

Base URL: change base_url to https://api.afaqy.pro if that is the environment the account lives on.

item.name: 0 · Login  (optional — skip if you already hold a token)

request.description:
Returns the access token and the account id.

Two values from this response are needed later:
  data.token    → the token used on every other call
  data.user.id  → the user_id sent when creating a report

Both are captured automatically into collection variables by the Tests script.

If you already have a token, skip this request and set {{token}} manually in the collection variables.

The report takes vehicle ids, NOT IMEIs. This call lists the account's vehicles so you can map an IMEI to its id.

The Tests script picks the unit whose imei equals {{imei}} and stores its id in {{unit_id}}. If {{imei}} is left empty, it simply takes the first unit so the rest of the chain still runs.

Raise limit or page with offset if the account holds more than 1000 vehicles.

exec: pm.test("At least one vehicle is visible to this account", () => pm.expect(list.length).to.be.above(0));
if (wanted) pm.test("The requested IMEI was found", () => pm.expect(hit && String(hit.imei)).to.eql(wanted));

item.name: 2 · List report templates  (where the codes and columns come from)

request.description:
Returns the report templates saved on the account, each with its code and its column definitions.

This is the same kind of catalog you get from /reports/lists: names, codes, formats and aggregation. A catalog never carries values — it describes the columns, it does not run the report.

Use it to confirm the exact code to send in step 3 (summary, summary_beta, summary_by_driver, and so on) and to copy the fields array verbatim if you want different columns than the ones pre-filled here.

request.description:
Runs the report and returns its id. It does NOT return rows.

Parameters that matter:
  code                    the report code from step 2
  fields                  the columns, in the same shape the catalog gives them
  resources               vehicle ids (not IMEIs) — add more ids to the array
  selected_resource_type  "units", or "drivers" for the by-driver variants
  date.from / date.to     YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS
  user_id                 from the login response (data.user.id)

The report id is captured into {{report_id}} automatically.

IMPORTANT: at this moment the rows do not exist yet. The report is generated asynchronously on the server. Go to step 4 before reading anything.

exec: pm.test("A report id came back", () => pm.expect(id, "data.id").to.be.a("string"));
pm.test("No rows are returned here — that is expected", () => pm.expect(true).to.be.true);

request.description:
THIS IS THE STEP THAT IS EASY TO MISS.

Returns how far the report has been generated:
  { "data": [ { "reportId": "...", "percentage": 100 } ] }

Call it repeatedly until percentage reaches 100. Only then do the rows exist.

If you read the data before that, /user_reports/data-summary answers with an empty data array, status_code 200 and message "success" — a completely valid response that looks like a failure. That is the single most common cause of "the report returns no data".

Running this collection with the Postman Runner makes this request loop on itself, waiting 3 seconds between attempts, up to 40 attempts (about 2 minutes). Clicking Send manually just performs one check — press it again until you see 100.

A large fleet or a long period takes longer. The report is stored server-side and is not lost, so keep polling.

exec: // تأخير 3 ثواني بين المحاولات لما الكولكشن بيتشغّل بالـ Runner
if (n > 0) { const t = Date.now() + 3000; while (Date.now() < t) { /* wait */ } }
const row = rows.find(r => String(r.reportId || r.report_id || r.id || "") === id) || rows[0];
const pct = row ? Number(row.percentage ?? row.percent) : null;
console.log("attempt " + n + " → " + (pct === null ? "no percentage field" : pct + "%"));
console.warn("No percentage field in the response — continuing to the next step.");
// الحلقة: بنرجع لنفس الريكوست تاني (بيشتغل مع الـ Runner)
pm.execution.setNextRequest("4 · Wait for generation  (repeat until percentage = 100)");
postman.setNextRequest("4 · Wait for generation  (repeat until percentage = 100)");

item.name: 5 · Report Summary  →  aggregated, one row per vehicle

request.description:
The aggregated summary: one row per vehicle for the whole period.

The keys are the same field codes from the catalog — date, route_length, engine_work, move_duration, engine_idle, stop_duration, max_spd — so this is where Route Length: 70 km appears with its value rather than its definition.

If data comes back as an empty array here, it means one of exactly two things:
  1. Step 4 has not reached 100 yet. Go back and keep polling.
  2. The vehicles genuinely did not move during the period you asked for.
It does not mean the request or the permissions are wrong.

exec: if (!rows.length) console.warn("Empty: either generation is unfinished (step 4) or the vehicles did not move in this period.");

item.name: 6 · Report Data  →  the detail behind ONE vehicle

request.description:
The detailed rows for a single vehicle inside the report.

resource_id is the unit id — the same value you put in resources in step 3.

This is not the same data as step 5 in a different shape. Step 5 gives one aggregated row per vehicle; this gives the breakdown behind one of them.

Optional: the endpoint also accepts a filters object, for example { "filters": { "is_stream": false } }.

exec: console.log("detail rows for unit " + pm.collectionVariables.get("unit_id") + ": " + rows.length);

item.name: 7 · Export the same report to a file

request.description:
Returns the same result as a file. type accepts pdf, excel or html.

Note: newer builds of the web application call /user_reports/request-export with a format field instead of type, against the same report id. Both serve the same purpose; this collection uses the documented one.

Every create in step 3 stores a report on the account. While testing, remove it afterwards so the customer's report list stays clean.

Skip this if the report is one the customer actually wants to keep.
